scenarios.name: log_in_reverse
scenarios.note: Every event of a log arrives before the one it follows. Each waits; the inception is accepted, and one escrow pass accepts the rest in sequence order.

scenarios.name: gap_in_a_known_log
scenarios.note: An accepted log receives the event after next, which waits until the next one is accepted.

scenarios.name: out_of_order_and_partially_signed
scenarios.note: A two-of-two interaction arrives early with one signature. Once the event before it is accepted, it moves to the partially signed escrow, and its second signature completes it.

scenarios.name: out_of_order_with_a_bad_signature
scenarios.note: An early event signed by a key that is not the identifier's waits, since nothing can be verified before the events it follows; once they are accepted its signature fails and it is dropped.

scenarios.name: out_of_order_delegated_rotation
scenarios.note: A delegated rotation naming its anchoring event arrives before the interaction it follows. When retried, keripy offers it without the seal source couple, so it moves to the partially delegated escrow, where the anchor is found by walking the delegator's log.

scenarios.name: likely_duplicitous
scenarios.note: A basic prefix is its key, so a second inception committing to other next keys has the same prefix and contradicts the first; a second interaction at an accepted number does too. Both are kept aside, once each however often they are offered, and never accepted.
